I recommend learning Lean using Mathematics in Lean or one of the other resources listed here: https://leanprover-community.github.io/learn.html
Then just formalize a small result in the area of mathematics of your choice to really learn how to write Lean yourself. Perhaps that project exposes some missing lemmas in Mathlib, which you can upstream. I recommend to wait with more ambitious "contributing to Mathlib" projects after you've finished a small project in your own repository.
For someone already comfortable proving results, would you recommend any particular resource for getting better at writing theorem statements?

The two often go hand in hand, as you develop a feeling of what is a good statement by having experience in proving a lot of results. You can start picking up a theorem you like and that is not in Mathlib and try to formalise it. The review process will help making it better and will teach you a lot.
